narrative_purpose: The eclipse argument in one image: the same valley in full daylight and mid-eclipse, so the reader sees convection as something with a power supply that can be switched off - the tower slumping and the small cumulus, which live entirely on thermals, gone first.
subject: A diptych of the identical forested valley under a gas giant sky, the two halves matched view for view. In the daylight half, a tall boiling cloud tower stands over the trees with a scatter of small flat-based cumulus around it, all brightly lit. In the eclipse half, the same valley lies in deep amber-brown gloom: the great tower has lost its crisp boiling structure and slumped into a ragged, spreading, softening mass, the small cumulus have vanished entirely leaving clear sky where they were, and the gas giant above is a vast dark disc rimmed with a thin bright edge.
scene: The same rainforest valley minutes apart - once under full daylight, once with the primary star occulted by the gas giant.
camera: Identical framing in both halves, a middle-distance view across the valley with the sky occupying the upper two-thirds.
light: In the daylight half, bright directional sun with strong cloud modelling. In the eclipse half, an extremely dim amber-brown ambient wash with no directional source, the canopy losing all colour and the surviving cloud lit only by scattered edge light from the gas giant's rim.
palette: Daylight half in living teal, misty-cyan cloud and void-indigo sky. Eclipse half in dim amber-brown and desaturated grey-teal, the whole half markedly darker and lower in contrast.
style: Painterly comparison plate, two matched panels side by side, atmospheric and hand-painted, NOT a hard vector schematic and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: Moderate in both halves, with the crucial difference legible: crisp boiling cloud structure and small cumulus present on one side, slumped ragged cloud and empty sky on the other.
composition: Two equal panels split by a clean vertical seam, terrain and horizon aligned exactly across the seam so the eye compares the sky rather than the land, with plain dim sky in each panel for callouts.
consistency_notes: Both halves must be recognisably the same valley from the same viewpoint; only the light and the clouds change. The disappearance of the small cumulus in the eclipse half is the teaching detail and must be obvious.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no panel numbers, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no differing viewpoint between halves
